{{Hatnote|For the GEMP format, see [[Sealed]].}}
'''Sealed Deck''' is [[Decipher]]'s basic sealed-play tournament format for Star Wars CCG: players open unopened product at the event, trade away the cards of the other side, and build a 40-card deck. Decipher published it in 1996 as a non-sanctioned format and sanctioned it by 1998.<ref name="tg96">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/tournamentguide.pdf Organizer's Guide (Tournament Rules System, August 1996 Release)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219040510/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/tournamentguide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="overview98">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Tournaments], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717031138/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (1996)
* '''Card pool:''' one unopened Premiere starter deck per player; later any starter deck plus the packs the director names; 40-card decks
* '''In use:''' 1996 – 2002
* '''Also called:''' Sealed Deck Tournaments (1996);<ref name="tg96" /> the Decipher Sealed Deck Tournament Format (1999);<ref name="tg99">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/swtournamentguide/formats.html Tournament Guide, II. Formats], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990502214324/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/swtournamentguide/formats.html Internet Archive].</ref> the Sealed Deck tournament (2000);<ref name="tg00">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentguide/tournamenttypesandformats.html Official Tournament Guide, II. Tournament Types and Formats], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000109144553/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentguide/tournamenttypesandformats.html Internet Archive].</ref> Premiere Sealed (Players Committee)<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>
* '''GEMP:''' none. [[Sealed]] is a GEMP sealed-league format with its own product.

== Card pool ==
=== 1996–1999: one Premiere starter ===
In 1996: "By simply bringing one sealed starter deck to a tournament everyone will be playing with the 'fate' of the cards." Players are assigned Rebel or Imperial for the whole event; paired opponents open their decks and exchange all their cards of the other side, face down ("Yep, even those Vaders and Lukes!!!"); each player then has about 30 minutes to build a 40-card deck. No other cards may be brought in or traded, but players may swap with their unused cards between games. After the games the top Imperial and top Rebel play a final game, and players keep the cards they traded for.<ref name="tg96" />

The 1999 guide specified "unopened Premiere starter decks (limited or unlimited)": a 40-card deck "from the 60 cards they have", a minimum of three games plus a final confrontation between the highest-scoring Rebel and Imperial players, and deck adjustment one for one from the "20 unused sealed deck cards". It also allowed '''theme''' sealed decks: "Tournament directors may run 'theme' sealed deck tournaments (Hoth, Dagobah etc.) by providing additional expansion packs for each player. ... In these cases, deck size can be increased up to, but no more than, 60 cards. These sealed deck events will still be sanctioned and rated."<ref name="tg99" />

=== 2000–2002: starter decks and packs ===
From the 2000 guide the format covered all of Decipher's games: "A sealed deck tournament is played with unopened starter decks", and each player must "bring, purchase, or be provided with any deck-building materials required for the tournament, such as expansion packs, Warp or Jedi Packs." For Star Wars CCG the deck is 40 cards, games are 60 minutes, players keep one side throughout, and the event has at least three games and a final confrontation between the top Dark and top Light player.<ref name="tg00" /><ref name="tg02">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/tournamentguide-stswyj.asp Official Tournament Guide (Star Trek CCG, Star Wars CCG, Young Jedi CCG)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020220233154/http://tournaments.decipher.com/tournamentguide-stswyj.asp Internet Archive].</ref>

== History ==
In 1996 Decipher's guide listed "Sealed Deck Tournaments (Non-Sanctioned)" beside the sanctioned Swiss constructed system: "Decipher has put thought into this type of tournament and have play tested it for problems."<ref name="tg96" /> Its non-sanctioned page that year said "Decipher has devised tournament rules for sealed-deck, elimination, and simple-swiss events. While we are not currently sanctioning these types of tournaments, we do want to encourage them."<ref name="nonsanc96">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/nonsanctionedintro.html Non-sanctioned Introduction], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219012152/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/nonsanctionedintro.html Internet Archive].</ref>

By July 1998 "Three Tournament formats are sanctioned: Swiss, Junior Swiss, and Sealed Deck", with a separate Sealed Deck Command Card.<ref name="overview98" /> The [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] (1998) added the [[Enhanced Format Sealed Deck]].<ref name="otsd98">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/sealeddeck.htm Using the Star Wars Customizable Card Game Official Tournament Sealed Deck], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980506110410/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/sealeddeck.htm Internet Archive].</ref> The 1999 guide kept a separate rating for each of the three formats: "Playing in one type of tournament has no effect on a players ratings for the other two types."<ref name="tg99" /> A new tournament director had to "run a Sealed Deck tournament before becoming permanent."<ref name="tfaq99">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentfaq.html Tournament FAQ], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990901024748/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentfaq.html Internet Archive].</ref>

Later Decipher sealed formats were built on these rules: [[First Anthology Sealed]], [[EPP Overdrive]], [[OTSD Booster Draft]], [[Endor Draft]] ("the tournament reverts to the standard Decipher sealed deck format"),<ref name="endorrules">[http://www1.decipher.com/starwars/rules/endorrules.html Star Wars CCG – Endor Rules Supplement], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990915001027/http://www1.decipher.com/starwars/rules/endorrules.html Internet Archive].</ref> the [[Death Star II Booster Draft]] and [[Death Star II Sealed-Deck Starter Format]], and [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck (format)|Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]]. In 2001 Decipher's new Sprint ratings covered constructed play only: "there will not be a Sprint Rating for the Sealed Deck category."<ref name="changes2001">[http://decipher.com/tournaments/changes2001/index.html Additions to the 2001 Sanctioned Tournament Program], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010203173600/http://decipher.com/tournaments/changes2001/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The Players Committee's Alternate Format Tournament Guide keeps "Premiere Sealed" (one Premiere Starter Deck, sealed rules) and sets sealed game time at one minute per card in the deck.<ref name="afg" />
